messages:
support-jamie: FYI customer Acme reported sharp p99 latency spikes on /v1/generate starting ~15:02 UTC, some 504s. They've sent a sample request and a trace-id: trace-0x7a9b.
support-jamie: snippet from their request headers and body for repro: `model: rwd-gpt-large, seq_len: 2048, temperature: 0.0, streaming: true`
carla (oncall): Thanks Jamie. Dropping into triage — can you paste the request ID(s) and region? any user token?
support-jamie: request id req_20260317_1523, region: eu-west-1, user-org: acme-inc, customer is on Dedicated pool A (reserved). They say p50 OK, p99 spikes to 2.4s -> previously ~200ms.
ben: Opening runtime tail: `rwdctl logs --tenant acme-inc --since 20m --filter "req_20260317_1523"` shows repeated kv cache misses and some model OOM retries. Also saw a spike in batch sizes for long seq.
alice: If OOMs, runtime may be falling back to CPU and blowing latency. Immediate mitigation options: 1) circuit-breaker on that route (failfast above 800ms) 2) apply temporary rate-limit for the tenant 3) force fallback to quantized / smaller model variant that fits GPU memory.
carla (oncall): Agreed. Prioritize (2) and (3) for fastest customer relief. Ben can you push a per-tenant rate limit? e.g. 100rps -> 40rps.
ben: Doing rate-limit now: `rwdctl rate-limits set --tenant acme-inc --route /v1/generate --limit 40 --burst 80 --duration 600s --reason "p99 spike mitigation"`
deploy-bot: rate-limit update queued -> change-id rl-20260317-01, applied by policy-service (ok).
ben: Also staging a rollout to quantized variant: `rwdctl rollout create --route /v1/generate --model rwd-gpt-large-8bit --percent 100 --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"` this will use eu-west model variant that has lower memory footprint.
alice: Add circuit-breaker rule to circuit-breaker-policy: `max-latency-ms=800, failures-window=60s, threshold=10%` so we failfast and fall back to hosted lightweight model.
carla (oncall): Circuit-breaker applied, checkout: cb-20260317-01 (activated). Monitor p99 and error rates for next 10m.
ben: After rate-limit + quantized rollout + cb, customer reports p99 reduced to ~350ms and 0 504s in the last 5m.
support-jamie: Customer confirmed improved UX. They're still seeing occasional slow tails for long seqs, asking if we can recommend prompt trimming.
alice: Post-mitigation we should: 1) add tenant-specific caching of prefix tokens 2) schedule a model-resize to better match their seq distribution 3) propose an autoscale bump on Dedicated pool A or move hotspots to additional nodes/regions.
carla (oncall): Creating follow-up ticket and postmortem. Steps for postmortem: collect `rwdctl traces --trace trace-0x7a9b`, collect host GPU metrics, kernel OOM logs, and batching stats for the 30m window. Also document decision tree we used (rate-limit -> quantized rollout -> circuit-breaker).
ben: Repro notes for ENG: reproduce with a mix of very long sequences and bursty concurrency targeting Dedicated pool A; use `loadtest/seq-long.yml` with headers to simulate tenant.
carla (oncall): Adding SLO guardrail action items: - enforce tenant-level soft quotas that auto-throttle above sustained p95/p99 deltas - default route circuit-breakers with sane defaults in Dedicated - add automatic fallback model mapping for memory pressure (e.g. >70% GPU mem -> switch to 8bit variant)
alice: I'll draft a short internal playbook snippet for the support/SE teams with one-click commands we used. Will include rollback commands: `rwdctl rollout rollback --change-id rl-20260317-01` and `rwdctl rate-limits delete --id rl-20260317-01`.
support-jamie: Thanks all. Customer appreciated the quick fix. Leaving ticket open until postmortem and follow-ups are done. :thumbsup:
